entries.lesson_title: Convolution of a Unit Step with a Decaying Exponential
entries.core_move: Compute the convolution of a unit step with a decaying exponential by using the causal overlap interval to evaluate the integral and write the result as ((1 - $e^{-at}$)/a)$u(t)$.

entries.lesson_title: Step Response of a First-Order System
entries.core_move: Compute the step response of a first-order LTI system by convolving a unit-step input with a decaying-exponential impulse response and interpreting the result as a rising exponential toward steady state.
Set up the convolution of two one-sided exponentials by translating their unit-step supports into causal overlap bounds, multiplying the exponential terms, and preparing the integral for evaluation.
Compute the equal-exponent convolution of two one-sided exponentials by recognizing the repeated-exponent case and deriving the ramp-weighted exponential output from the causal overlap integral.
Compute the unequal-exponent convolution of two one-sided exponentials by evaluating the causal overlap integral and simplifying it into the scaled difference of exponentials.
Interpret causal convolution by connecting one-sided support and overlap bounds to the LTI output rule that only past input values weighted by the impulse response contribute at time t.
